title: Phase 0: Safety & Correctness
description: P0 priority — Fix critical safety bugs before any feature work. Includes: (1) Replace pkill -f with Treehouse.return() for workspace cleanup, (2) Add crash cleanup lifecycle with PeerCrashed event, (3) Add VerifyProfile-based verification before accept. All existing tests must pass. New safety tests required.

title: 0.1: Replace pkill -f with Treehouse.return()
description: DANGEROUS BUG: pkill -f regex pattern can match and kill current Claude session. Replace with Treehouse.return_if_lease() for workspace cleanup. PeerManager owns process lifecycle (terminate by PID), TreehouseAdapter owns workspace lifecycle (cleanup + release). Files: crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs (line 629), crates/anti-workspace/src/lib.rs. Verification: spawn peer → kill peer → verify worktree cleaned → verify current session unaffected.

title: 0.2: Crash cleanup lifecycle
description: Current: reaper marks CRASHED but no cleanup. Target: PeerCrashDetected → capture exit info → Treehouse.return (cleanup) → persist evidence → notify Lead → Lead decides retry/replace/abort. Files: crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs (crash handler), crates/anti-core/src/events.rs (new event types). Must include: PID liveness check, exit code capture, workspace lease release, crash evidence persistence.

title: 0.3: VerifyProfile-based verification
description: Add verify stage before accept. VerifyProfile enum: Full (fmt+clippy+test+build), Check (fmt+clippy+test), Test (cargo test), Build (cargo build), Named (from config). NOT arbitrary commands — prevents execution escape hatch. VerificationResult: status, test_output, build_output, diagnostics, git_diff, claims_verified. Files: crates/anti-core/src/work.rs, crates/anti-daemon/src/ipc.rs, crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs, crates/anti-cli/src/main.rs. Success: verify produces evidence, state becomes Verified, accept requires Verified.

title: Phase 1: Execution Architecture
description: P1 — 2 weeks. Staged task state machine (RECEIVED→EXPLORED→PLANNED→EXECUTING→VERIFYING→ACCEPTED), EvidenceRecord model (git diff, test output, build output, diagnostics), Writer-Verifier separation via disposition contracts. Depends on Phase 0 safety fixes.

title: 1.1: Staged task state machine
description: Expand WorkItemState from 7 to 12+ states: RECEIVED→EXPLORED→PLANNED→EXECUTING→EXECUTED→VERIFYING→VERIFIED→ACCEPTED. Failed/Rejected paths: EXECUTING→FAILED, VERIFYING→REJECTED→FIXING→EXECUTING, EXHAUSTED→CANCELLED. Files: crates/anti-core/src/work.rs, crates/anti-daemon/src/store.rs (migration). Tests: staged pipeline transitions, verify fail triggers fix loop bounded by max_revisions.

title: 1.2: EvidenceRecord model
description: Replace simple SHA-256 EvidenceRef with comprehensive EvidenceRecord: artifact_sha256, test_output, test_exit_code, build_output, build_exit_code, lint_output, diagnostics, git_sha, git_diff, git_status, claims (Vec<ClaimVerification>). Files: crates/anti-core/src/work.rs, crates/anti-daemon/src/store.rs (new table). Migration: evidence_records table with all fields.

title: 1.3: Disposition contracts (basic)
description: DispositionContract struct: name, allowed_tools, denied_tools, can_approve_own_work, requires_evidence, max_concurrent. Engineer: read/write/test, cannot self-approve. Scout: read/search, cannot modify. Reviewer: inspect/test/challenge, cannot silently modify. ProofAuditor: read/test/inspect, cannot modify. Files: crates/anti-core/src/disposition.rs (new). Tests: each disposition's tool access.

title: Phase 2: SLP-Native Orchestration
description: P2 — 2 weeks. Formal disposition contracts with tool enforcement, lifecycle event bus (15+ event types), task scheduler. Depends on Phase 1 execution architecture.

title: 2.1: Disposition contracts (formal enforcement)
description: Runtime tool enforcement: PeerManager checks DispositionContract before allowing tool execution. Denied tools → block with clear error. can_approve_own_work → false for Engineer. requires_evidence → true for ProofAuditor. Max concurrent limits per disposition. Files: crates/anti-core/src/disposition.rs, crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs (tool guard). Tests: each disposition's enforcement.

title: 2.2: Lifecycle event bus
description: EventBus with typed events: PeerSpawned/Ready/Crashed/Stopped, TaskReceived/Executing/Completed/Failed, VerificationStarted/Passed/Failed, WorkspaceAcquired/Released/Cleaned, LeadHandoff. Handler dispatch, recovery triggers. Files: crates/anti-core/src/events.rs (expand), crates/anti-daemon/src/bus.rs (new). Tests: event emission, handler execution, recovery trigger.

title: Phase 3: Scheduling & Routing
description: P3 — 2 weeks. Config-based model routing (disposition × complexity → capability tier → provider config), parallel scheduler (resource-aware, dependency-aware). Depends on Phase 2 orchestration.

title: 3.1: Config-based model routing
description: CapabilityTier enum: Lightweight/Standard/Heavyweight. Route resolution: disposition × complexity → capability → model (from provider config). ProviderConfig loaded from .anti_subagent/providers.toml. NOT hard-coded model names in core. Files: crates/anti-core/src/routing.rs (new). Tests: routing resolution, config loading.

title: 3.2: Parallel scheduler
description: Scheduler with max_concurrent_peers (configurable), DagGraph for task dependencies, ResourceMonitor (CPU/RAM). Schedule: build dependency graph → find independent sets → check resources → assign peers → return parallel groups. Files: crates/anti-daemon/src/scheduler.rs (new). Tests: scheduling with dependencies, resource limits, parallel groups.

title: Phase 4: Reliability
description: P4 — 2 weeks. Restart recovery (SQLite → PID liveness → cleanup → notify), Lead handoff (context degradation → experience transfer → new Lead), Supervisor on-demand. Depends on Phase 3 scheduling.

title: 4.1: Restart recovery
description: Daemon restart: find RUNNING sessions → check PID liveness → dead → mark CRASHED → Treehouse.return (cleanup) → persist crash evidence → emit PeerCrashed event. Files: crates/anti-daemon/src/main.rs (recovery logic). Tests: restart with live peer, restart with dead peer, restart with missing workspace.

title: 4.2: Lead handoff
description: LeadHandoff: from_lead, to_lead, reason (ContextDegradation/ManualHandoff/SupervisorDecision), context (active_tasks, pending_reviews, decisions, open_questions), lessons. Triggered by: context degradation after 5-7 compactions, manual command, Supervisor decision. Files: crates/anti-daemon/src/handoff.rs (new). Tests: handoff preserves context, lessons transfer, new Lead resumes correctly.
